c.tagline: A red-ochre Saharan oasis town of mudbrick architecture, palm groves, and a shimmering salt lake

taxi.fareNote: Most sightseeing is arranged as a half or full-day tour rather than metered taxi rides

emergency.note: Dial 17 for police and 14 for medical/fire emergencies; French is more useful than English with dispatchers

walk: The ksar and market area are walkable; the salt lake viewpoint and surrounding dune villages require a car or organized tour

safety.safety: Generally calm and welcoming to visitors, though remote; check current travel advisories for southern Algeria before visiting
safety.crime: Low crime; main risks relate to desert heat and remoteness rather than crime

hood_landmark.Old Ksar (Red Town): Timimoun's red ochre mudbrick old town
hood_landmark.Sebkha Viewpoint: The shimmering salt lake sunset viewpoint
hood_landmark.Palm Oasis: The palm grove and traditional foggara irrigation channels

avoid.reason: Do not head into the open desert or toward border zones without authorized guides — surrounding Saharan areas are under security restrictions and often require police-notified itineraries.

hood_desc: The town's iconic red mudbrick old quarter, with distinctive Sudanese-influenced architecture found nowhere else in Algeria.
The dramatic salt lake bordering the oasis, best visited at sunset when the white crust glows pink and orange.
The palm grove sustaining the town, still watered by an ancient underground foggara canal system.
The commercial center with the covered market and most hotels and restaurants.
A nearby red-clay village a short drive away, similar in style to Timimoun but far less visited.

water.note: Stick to bottled water in Saharan oasis towns.

transit.sys: Local taxis and guide-arranged vehicles; no formal bus network
transit.pay: Cash to the driver or guide
transit.map: Not centrally published; hotels and tour agencies arrange transport
transit.note: A local guide is recommended for dune excursions and visits to outlying ksour villages

transport.air: Timimoun Airport (TMX), about 5 km from town
transport.bus: Long-distance buses connect to Adrar and onward to Algiers
transport.car: The N51 highway connects Timimoun to the regional road network

net.m: Moderate 3G/4G in town, no coverage in the surrounding desert
net.w: Wifi available in some hotels but often slow
net.gb: ~$5-10 for a prepaid tourist SIM (passport required to register)
net.fwn: Wifi available in central hotels, though unreliable
net.ap: A Mobilis or Djezzy prepaid SIM, registered with your passport

tip.s: 10% is customary and appreciated for desert guides
tip.r: Rounding up or 5-10% is appreciated, not obligatory
